bc_p_heartbreak_hotel.blurb: Heartbreak Hotel is a small cluster of boulders in the forest at the foot of the Stawamus Chief, one pocket of Squamish's Grand Wall Boulders. Its fifteen problems stretch from an easy warm-up to V10, with a comfortable middle of V1 to V4 and a handful of hard lines between V7 and V10. The setting is a shady, tree-filled maze, and landings can be awkward because of roots and loose rock, so a few smaller pads work better than one big one. It is the first block you meet on the trail, which makes it a handy stop for a mixed group.
bc_p_heartbreak_hotel.approach: From the old Psych Ledge road, take the third trail that leaves it just beyond the outhouse. It passes the Animal Magnetism boulder and a short scramble beside the Cacodemon boulder, and Heartbreak Hotel is the first block you reach.

bc_high_five_boulders.blurb: A tight group of boulders near Powell River on the Sunshine Coast, tucked beneath the High Five cliff. The fifteen problems here are all fairly approachable: most fall between V2 and V4, with a couple of easier V1s and two V5s at the top end. It is a good spot for climbers who want a session of moderate problems in the trees rather than a hard-project venue. Expect a forested, low-key feel and the usual need for pads and a spotter.
bc_high_five_boulders.approach: About 20 minutes uphill on foot from the main roadside pullout. A vehicle with good clearance can continue closer, leaving only a short flat walk through the trees.

bc_octopus_garden.blurb: Octopus' Garden is a crack-focused crag in the Smoke Bluffs, the cluster of small cliffs on the edge of Squamish. Nearly all of its fifteen routes are trad, with a single sport line. The grades lean friendly: most climbs are 5.8, with a few at 5.9 and 5.10, then a handful of harder pitches in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. Lines follow long, sinuous cracks, and the wall can also be top-roped, so it suits those learning to place gear. The forested, shaded setting and its distance from the parking area tend to keep it quieter than neighbouring walls.

bc_up_among_the_firs.blurb: Up Among the Firs is one sector of Murrin Park, a collection of crags just south of Squamish beside Highway 99. It holds fifteen single-pitch routes, ten trad and five sport. The grades sit in the middle of the range: a few at 5.7 to 5.9, a big group of 5.10s, and several at 5.11, so it works best for climbers already comfortable on steady leads. The park is known for quiet corners even on busy weekends, and the lake nearby is handy for cooling off afterwards.
